trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Deep Speech.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
In the days of the First War, an era that marked the initial curiosity of myriad nations towards Luyarnha, a scattering of Dwarves from far-flung reaches of the world found themselves irresistibly drawn to this beleaguered city, a crucible of turmoil and devastation. Amongst those who joined the cause, the majority were mercenaries, whilst others were noble souls seeking to lend aid, and finally a few harbored ambitions of extracting wealth from the faltering nation. As the tides of war shifted, those Dwarves who had chosen to engage in the struggle were offered homes and gold in gratitude for their service, persuading many to remain, forever entwining their destinies with that of the city. The few families that had settled in Luyarnha commenced the trade of precious ores, using their connection to their homeland and harnessing the sophisticated railway system already in place there, thus expanding it within the very walls of the city-state.

Far removed from the splendorous halls of their ancestral kingdoms, the dwarves of Luyarnha have undergone a profound transformation, the likes of which none of their kin foresaw. These once grand merchants perpetrated a sin—coveting that which was not rightfully theirs—and for this dereliction of morality, they begot a curse of unspeakable malevolence, condemning their blood to the compelled service of He Who Lies Dreaming.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 94 (Indie)

trait.name: The Cardinal Sin
trait.text: "Thou shalt not steal," a dwarven tenet as ancient as their race itself, yet one that an unfortunate number amongst their kin failed to honor. In their homeland, theft was deemed a cardinal sin, punishable to the utmost extent of their laws, at times even by death. Those dwarves harboring avaricious desires deep within, biding their time for the perfect moment to sin unpunished, saw their opportunity amidst the war-torn Luyarnha. Concealed within the ranks of their wellintentioned brethren, they entered Luyarnha only to scatter, some swept away by the tide of war, but those who survived coalesced into marauding bands preying upon the vulnerable. Their plundering persisted until they dared to trespass upon a dwelling that should have remained undisturbed, its walls etched with an archaic language, and its occupant patiently awaiting their intrusion. Unwittingly, they had captured the attention of an entity far more formidable than they could fathom. On that ill-fated day, the lives of these dwarves were irrevocably altered, as they metamorphosed into the Y'ha-nthlei, the enigmatic Deep Ones, a destiny far grimmer than death.

trait.name: The Long Night
trait.text:
A multitude of dwarves had chosen to dwell within the Waterfront district, where the ships dock lay, their shared culture fostering a harmonious coexistence. In a mutually beneficial relationship, they imbued the district with distinct dwarven elements, adding to the gothic architectural landscape and bequeathing the area with a unique aesthetic that endures to this day.
	Yet, the enigmatic Deep Ones, though but a minority amongst Luyarnha's dwarven populace, insidiously encroached upon the Waterfront district. They renounced their thieving ways and instead, embarked upon a sinister campaign of abduction, forcibly indoctrinating their unsuspecting brothers into the worship of their slumbering sovereign, slowly corrupting the inherent goodness that once thrived within the district's walls.
	One fateful night, the Deep Ones executed a vast, coordinated kidnapping, spiriting away hundreds of dwarves in the span of a single, darkened eve — the Long Night. Wanted posters soon plastered the city streets, while the cursed bloods and scions marshaled their forces, and the church dispatched their hunters, all determined to unearth the truth behind the sudden, inexplicable vanishings. And, as mysteriously as they had vanished, the dwarves reappeared, slumbering upon the shoreline, fragrant with the potent aroma of alcohol. The House of Blood's interrogations yielded naught, and soon town criers announced the incident a grand dwarven celebration of the new lunar year, characterized by inebriation and disorientation, leaving the dwarves with no clear memory of the events. Yet from that day forth, a heightened presence of hunters and wardens patrol the district, either to impart a sense of security or, perhaps, because those in authority are privy to some unsettling secret.
	Ever since, the dwarves of Luyarnha have felt a disquieting shift in their lives. Though many remain untouched by the insidious corruption of the Deep Ones' cult, blissfully ignorant of its existence, uncertainty lingers in the air as to how long this fragile equilibrium will endure, before another Long Night befall the remnants of dwarvenkind within Luyarnha, reducing them to nothing but enslaved thralls.

trait.name: Raiders To Smugglers
trait.text:
The Scions, scientists skilled in melding life through electricity to craft manikins and other constructs, grew increasingly reliant upon trade, their experiments demanding gold, mithril and other alloys capable of withstanding the forces of lightning. Yet, as the Scourge surged anew and Luyarnha was once more besieged, the Scions found themselves in dire straits, the resources essential to their groundbreaking research now perilously scarce.
	In this desperate hour, the Y'ha-nthlei emerged, their singular mastery of smuggling enabling them to procure vital materials from beyond the beleaguered city. Young Deep Ones, proficient in navigation and seamanship, who retained greater control over their faculties, could alone navigate the hazardous routes into and out of Luyarnha, defying the lockdown imposed on the city. These enigmatic dwarves proved invaluable to the Scions, and in exchange for their services, the Y'hanthlei furthered their inscrutable goals, burrowing ever deeper into the city's fabric, drawing the unwitting populace closer to the unfathomable depths of their eldritch master's influence.
	Owing to the secretive nature of the Deep Ones and the waning number of "ordinary" dwarves, the race is seen less frequently by the city's denizens. Although they continue to trade and offer their expertise in architectural planning and resource gathering, these skills diminished in importance as the Scourge expanded. Many dwarves adapted their inherent talents to farming, their stout physique ideally suited for laboring within the town's greenhouses, striving alongside others to produce sustenance for the populace. A handful of thrill-seeking dwarves enlisted in the ranks of the hunters, unfortunately a sizeable portion of battle-hardened dwarves unburdened by scruples have already fallen under the thrall of the Y'hanthlei, now toiling to fulfill the sinister objectives of their eldritch master rather than fighting for freedom.

trait.name: His Blessing
trait.text: Their very nature was irrevocably altered, much like those who dwell beneath the fathomless depths of the ocean; relinquished was their mortality, traded for the cold embrace of eternal slavery. They would never perish, but instead live out their days alongside He who had walked the earth long before the advent of humankind and would endure their demise for wretched ages, forever bound as pawns in the insidious machinations of their infinite master. Their tragic fate—wrought by their own rapacious avarice—is the exorbitant price they paid for their crime, and one they cannot escape.

trait.name: Deceptive Appearance
trait.text: This curse has warped their flesh, normally so averse to magic, and created within them gates of eldritch arcane, imparting them with the peculiar ability to cloak their twisted forms, using illusions that can deceive even the keenest adventurers into seeing them as bona fide dwarves.

trait.name: Accursed Immortality
trait.text: Despite possessing full control of their mental faculty from a young age, their physical form twists and contorts as the impossible weight of the gift of the Slumbering One scrapes them minute after minute. Their once sturdy limbs warp and bend in grotesque fashion, their eyes become sunken and hollow, and their skin takes on a sickly gray pallor. The sanity of their younger days begins to slip away, leaving them at the mercy of His malevolent dreams and to dwell within their once dwarven flesh. This destiny—a fate more dreadful than death—is something that their aging mind anticipates with glee.

trait.name: Aberration
trait.text: Your creature type is aberration, rather than humanoid.

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Charisma score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Deep One Dwarves mature much faster than humans, reaching maturity at the age of 10. They cannot die of old age; instead their aging mind progressively loses grip over their body, turning them into brainless servants of He Who Lies Dreaming when they reach 50 years of age.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Dwarves stand between 4 and 5 feet tall and average about 150 pounds. Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 25 feet and you have a swimming speed of 25 feet.

trait.name: Otherworldly Resilience
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against cold damage.

trait.name: Illusory Body
trait.text: Although your body is covered in tentacles, clams, seashells, and other eldritch appendages, you are covered by an illusion which makes you appear like a normal hill dwarf to others. You can use an action to turn this illusion on or off. Other Deep Ones can see through this illusion.

trait.name: Sailor Training
trait.text: You have proficiency with cleavers, tridents, and firearms.

trait.name: Amphibious
trait.text: You can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Cosmic Knowledge
trait.text: Whenever you make an History check related to the origin of an eldritch item or construction, you are considered proficient in the History skill and add double your proficiency bonus to the check, instead of your normal proficiency bonus.

trait.name: Guiding Light
trait.text: You know the dancing lights cantrip. Charisma is your spellcasting modifier for the spell.

trait.name: The Dreamer's Curse
trait.text: Your mind is clouded by the dreams of the Slumbering One, and you find it hard to discern between reality and dream. You have disadvantage on saving throws against illusions.

trait.name: Fathomless Limb
trait.text:
Your body has been altered beyond recognition by the Slumbering One, giving you one of the following body alterations:

	• Coiling Arm. Your arm is nothing but a writhing mass of tentacles that flail the air. On your turn, after hitting an enemy with a melee attack, you can attempt to grapple them as a bonus action (normal grappling restrictions apply).

	• Brutal Pincers. Your forearm—a massive pincer—is a natural weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. It you hit with it, you deal piercing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike. If you are targeting a creature you are grappling, the damage die becomes a d10 instead. You cannot use this arm to make any precise hand manipulation.

	• Mucoid Extremities. Your hands and feet are palmed and covered in cups. Your swimming speed increases to 30 feet, and you gain a climbing speed of 20 feet.

trait.name: The Dreamer's Gifts (Optional Trait at the GM's Discretion)
trait.text:
Your devotion to the cosmic being that warped your species is rewarded. Starting at level 5, you gain the following benefits:

	• Whenever you fail an ability check or saving throw, you can draw upon your master's powers to succeed instead. Once you've used this ability, you can't do so again until the Dreamer has replaced one of your d20 rolls with a 1. The GM decides when this unfortunate moment happens.

	• You are immune to the curse of the Slumbering Moon.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common, Deep Speech, and Dwarvish.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
With a touch of gold, a breath of lightning, and hours of meticulous welding and articulation, a manikin is 'born'. Often called 'marionettes' or living dolls', these creatures were originally the creations of the Scions, a Luyarnhian sect who seek to craft a force capable of protecting the city. Though each manikin looks different—indeed, they can resemble any race—the thin golden stitching that joins the plates of their artificial skin is a giveaway that the creature is a manmade creation.

Custodians are built as an alternative to golems and commonly find use as butlers, laborers, and cannon fodder. Sentient beings, they are sworn to defend the person —or customer— for whom they were created. The death of their owner often leaves them aimless, wandering the world like masterless hedge knights in search of meaning.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 106 (Indie)

trait.name: Free Will
trait.text: Inscribed on human eyes inside their skulls are the instructions which all manikin obey. More often than not, this includes a safety system that ensures adherence to the law and prevents a manikin turning on their master. In some cases, a crafter might even cause the manikin to feel love for their creator. Conceived as animate objects capable of carrying out the instructions, manikin who express thoughts of self-liberation are often disposed of before these thoughts turn into acts. Though the Scions intentions were initially noble, playing god has given them a taste for power and they have no intention of granting free will to their animated servants.

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Strength score increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: As they are not alive, Manikins do not age. However, their materials slowly lose their magic essence over time, meaning they will ultimately lose control over their entire body and turn back into inanimate objects.

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: You are a Humanoid. You are also considered a Construct for any prerequisite or effect that requires you to be a Construct.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Manikins can be small puppets or imposing wardens. You are Medium or Small. You choose the size when you select this race.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Born To Serve
trait.text: Manikins are made to be unable to hate or resent their creators. This lapse in judgment affects you in all circumstances. You have disadvantage on Insight checks.

trait.name: Lightning Heart
trait.text: Lightning Heart. You have resistance to lightning damage.

trait.name: Living Material
trait.text: Manikins don't need to eat, drink, or breathe and are immune to the poisoned condition. In addition, their metallic mind is incorruptible, they have advantage on saving throws against madness.

trait.name: Modular Gold Plating
trait.text:
Your body has built-in defensive layers, which determine your armor class. You gain no AC benefit from wearing armor, but if you are using a shield, you apply its bonus as normal. Through 8 hours of work in a specialized workshop, you can alter your defensive layers to the Medium Armor or Heavy Armor options below, or back into your Unarmored state.

• Prerequisite: Unarmored; AC = 11 + your Dexterity modifier

• Prerequisite: Medium Armor proficiency; 13 + your Dexterity modifier (maximum of 2) or Strength modifier (maximum of 3). Choose which modifier when you gain this state.

• Prerequisite: Heavy Armor proficiency; AC = 16 + your Strength modifier (maximum of 2).

If you use your Strength modifier for AC, you have disadvantage on Stealth checks.

trait.name: Careful Defender
trait.text: Designed to protect, you are adept at throwing yourself in the way of harm to shield others. When a creature within 5 feet of you is targeted by an attack, you can use your reaction to jump in front of it. If the creature is willing, you switch places with it, becoming the target of the attack instead. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

trait.name: Powerful Build
trait.text: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read and write Common.

trait.text: As they are not alive, Manikins do not age. However, their materials slowly lose their magic essence over time, meaning they will ultimately lose control over their entire body and turn back into inanimate objects.

trait.name: Creature Type
trait.text: You are a Humanoid. You are also considered a Construct for any prerequisite or effect that requires you to be a Construct.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Manikins can be small puppets or imposing wardens. You are Medium or Small. You choose the size when you select this race.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Born To Serve
trait.text: Manikins are made to be unable to hate or resent their creators. This lapse in judgment affects you in all circumstances. You have disadvantage on Insight checks.

trait.name: Lightning Heart
trait.text: Lightning Heart. You have resistance to lightning damage.

trait.name: Living Material
trait.text: Manikins don't need to eat, drink, or breathe and are immune to the poisoned condition. In addition, their metallic mind is incorruptible, they have advantage on saving throws against madness.

trait.name: Modular Gold Plating
trait.text:
Your body has built-in defensive layers, which determine your armor class. You gain no AC benefit from wearing armor, but if you are using a shield, you apply its bonus as normal. Through 8 hours of work in a specialized workshop, you can alter your defensive layers to the Medium Armor or Heavy Armor options below, or back into your Unarmored state.

• Prerequisite: Unarmored; AC = 11 + your Dexterity modifier

• Prerequisite: Medium Armor proficiency; 13 + your Dexterity modifier (maximum of 2) or Strength modifier (maximum of 3). Choose which modifier when you gain this state.

• Prerequisite: Heavy Armor proficiency; AC = 16 + your Strength modifier (maximum of 2).

If you use your Strength modifier for AC, you have disadvantage on Stealth checks.

trait.name: Inconspicuous Appearance
trait.text: You are a master at blending into your surroundings. You gain proficiency in the Stealth skill and with disguise kits.

trait.name: Embedded Armament
trait.text: You can have up to two melee weapons embedded within your body. Each weapon must have either the finesse or light property. During a short rest, you can remove one or both weapons and exchange them for other appropriate weapons you are holding. As a bonus action, you can draw or stow one or both of these embedded weapons. You can't be disarmed of your embedded weapons, short of having your arms cut off.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read and write Common.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
With a touch of gold, a breath of lightning, and hours of meticulous welding and articulation, a manikin is 'born'. Often called 'marionettes' or living dolls', these creatures were originally the creations of the Scions, a Luyarnhian sect who seek to craft a force capable of protecting the city. Though each manikin looks different—indeed, they can resemble any race—the thin golden stitching that joins the plates of their artificial skin is a giveaway that the creature is a manmade creation.

Made to entertain, thespians bring joy to nobles, the clergy, and commoners alike. The only type of manikin designed without lethal intent, these manikins' bodies are supported by invisible, intangible strings, allowing them to move seemingly in defiance of physics. As the plague worsened, the Scions bent their will to producing manikins capable of combating the Scourge, and so the number of thespians has steadily dwindled.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 106 (Indie)

trait.name: Free Will
trait.text: Inscribed on human eyes inside their skulls are the instructions which all manikin obey. More often than not, this includes a safety system that ensures adherence to the law and prevents a manikin turning on their master. In some cases, a crafter might even cause the manikin to feel love for their creator. Conceived as animate objects capable of carrying out the instructions, manikin who express thoughts of self-liberation are often disposed of before these thoughts turn into acts. Though the Scions intentions were initially noble, playing god has given them a taste for power and they have no intention of granting free will to their animated servants.

trait.name: Ethereal Strings
trait.text: As a bonus action, you can attach yourself to a willing creature you can see within 30 feet of you via a set of immaterial strings for 1 hour. If the creature you're attached to doesn't use all of its movement on its turn (if it has multiple movement speeds, pick the highest one), you can use your reaction at the end of the turn to move a number of feet equal to its remaining movement. Once you attach yourself to a creature in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

trait.text: You can speak, read and write Common.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Scourgebornes should not exist. They are an abomination of the world, a vile curse placed on those who peered beyond the veil and succumbed to madness. Their twisted appearance is but a mirror of the darkest recesses of their personality. All sentient creatures harbor a monster within their soul—the dark of you that resents your neighbor for having a better life than you, that hates your friends when they ignore you, that wishes to harm those that wrong you—most are fortunate enough to be able to hide this monster behind a mask of false virtues. Not the Scourgeborne.
	Their curse has taken all the most twisted aspects of their personality and laid them bare for the whole world to see. They wear this disfigured appearance every day;
the more resentment, hatred and anger one possesses, the more monstrous the appearance.
	Many view this Eldritch revelation as a curse - a curse that drives one to slip deeper and deeper into the depths of depravity until nothing but the monster remains. Yet, many refuse to let it break them - with their innermost darkness now visible, they have no choice but to accept it. It is said that accepting a fault is the first step in correcting it. Those scourgeborne who embrace their inner monster, but refuse to let it rule them, often become messianic heroes within the walls of Luyarnha, attempting to redeem the entire world with their actions, and perhaps one day, themselves.

Your subrace is dictated by an eldritch curse, which doesn't seem to follow a clear reasoning, although it seems that whatever aspect of your personality is most depraved will influence the beast that emerges.

The person who schemes and creates a web of lies around themselves is, unsurprisingly, bound to turn into an aranea. Also known as half-spiders, these scourgeborne differ from others—though many turn, few retain their sanity. Amongst the scourgeborne, araneas are the least trusted, their appearance revealing their former—or current—manipulative personality. Although most citizens understand the need for violence, especially in Luyarnha, none tolerate deception and betrayal.

Source:	Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt p. 109 (Indie)

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Constitution and Intelligence scores increase by 1 and one ability score of your choice increases by 1.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: Scourgeborne are made not born. This means that they mature at the same rate as the race they originally belonged to.

trait.name: Size
trait.text: Scourgeborne are about the same size and build as humans. Your size is Medium.

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Feral Limbs
trait.text: The horns, claws or fangs that you have developed due to your mutation are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal piercing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike. If your alignment is Evil, your feral side is more dominant and the die size for your unarmed strikes increases to a d8.

trait.name: Eldritch Curse
trait.text: Your curse is not something mere mortals can undo. You are immune to any spell that would alter your form. (e.g., alter self, polymorph...)

trait.name: Born of Madness
trait.text:
Your body is not the one you were born with, but rather the consequence to your exposure to eldritch madness:

	• If your alignment is Good, you gain control over your darkest impulses. You have advantage on saving throws against madness.

	• If your alignment is Evil you let the depraved monster within you influence you. You have disadvantage on saving throws against madness but gain a bonus to Dexterity saving throws equal to your Proficiency bonus.

trait.name: Spider Climb
trait.text: You have a climbing speed of 30 feet. In addition, you can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check. You can only do so for a number of minutes equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended minutes when you finish a long rest.

trait.name: Web Spit
trait.text: As a bonus action, you hurl sticky web at a creature within 60 feet of you; it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier) or be restrained by the webbing. As an action, the restrained target can make a Strength check against the DC, bursting the webbing and freeing itself on a success. The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed (AC 10; HP equal to 3 times your proficiency bonus; vulnerability to fire damage; immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage). Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language of your choice.

trait.name: Tattered Wings

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
The summer elves are well-known for their hedonistic and sociable nature. Living life to the fullest, they constantly seek new experiences and pleasures. These elves embody the teachings of their patron deity, Òigridh, the Lady of Summer and Queen of Fire, who champions the pursuit of positive emotions and hope.
	Their vibrant and luxurious lifestyle often leads summer elves to confront penumbral creatures such as penumbral envys, greeds, gluttonies, and lusts. Driven by disdain for the Ungods' corruption of emotions, they strive to bring positivity and hope to those they encounter. Engaging with penumbral creatures is an inherent part of their journey to promote new experiences and combat the forces of darkness.
	Summer elves are particularly drawn to the company of humans, finding their constant change and strong emotions captivating. They often live and travel between human cities, embracing their dynamic nature and thriving in their diverse communities. This proximity leads to most of the half-elves in Tanares being half-summer elves, a testament to the deep connection formed between them.
	As natural wanderers, many summer elves become traders and merchants. Their deity, Òigridh, views trade as an act that brings happiness to both parties involved, considering it an essential means of spreading positivity and weakening the Ungods. In their travels, summer elves explore new experiences, including diverse forms of art, unique individuals, captivating music, and exotic drinks. They often establish connections and relationships with various cultures, enriching their knowledge and understanding of the world.
	Summer elves typically exhibit darker skin tones and beautiful black hair, often kept long and styled in intricate ways. Their attire is as exuberant and expressive as their personalities, frequently featuring fine, vibrant clothing that showcases their love for art and emotion. This striking appearance reflects their inner passion and the vivacity they infuse into every aspect of their lives.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 16 (Indie)

trait.name: Ability Score Increase
trait.text: Your Charisma score is increased by 1. You can also increase one other ability score of your choice by 1, except for Dexterity and Charisma.

trait.name: Age
trait.text: A Tanarean elf can live up to twenty thousand years. They still reach adulthood at the age of 100, but never show any loss of health or sign of old age until their final days.

trait.name: Size
trait.text:
Elves range from under 5 to over 6 feet tall and have slender builds. Your size is Medium.

To set your height and weight randomly, start with rolling a size modifier:

Size modifier = 2d6
Height = 4 feet + 5 inches + your size modifier in inches
Weight in pounds = 75 + (1d6 × your size modifier)

trait.name: Speed
trait.text: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

trait.name: Darkvision
trait.text: Accustomed to twilit forests and the night sky, you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

trait.name: Keen Senses
trait.text: You have proficiency in the Perception skill.

trait.name: Fey Ancestry
trait.text: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put you to sleep.

trait.name: Trance
trait.text:
Elves don't need to sleep. Instead, they meditate deeply, remaining semiconscious, for 4 hours a day. (The Common word for such meditation is "trance.") While meditating, you can dream after a fashion; such dreams are actually mental exercises that have become reflexive through years of practice. After resting in this way, you gain the same benefit that a human does from 8 hours of sleep.
	If you meditate during a long rest, you finish the rest after only 4 hours. You otherwise obey all the rules for a long rest; only the duration is changed.

trait.name: Ancestral Summer Magic
trait.text: Through your people's tradition and passionate spirit, you gain access to spells to influence others. You know one enchantment cantrip of your choice. When you reach 5th level, you learn a 2nd-level enchantment spell of your choice and can cast it once with this trait. At 7th level, you can cast the tongues spell once with this trait. You regain the ability to cast these spells when you finish a long rest. During character creation, you choose whether your spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma or Intelligence.

trait.name: Languages
trait.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Elvish. Elvish is fluid, with subtle intonations and intricate grammar. Elven literature is rich and varied, and their songs and poems are famous among other races. Many bards learn their language so they can add Elvish ballads to their repertoires.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
The spring elves of Tanares are a deeply spiritual and dedicated group, entrusted with the critical task of caring for the ten remaining Mother Trees in the Sindile Forest. These mighty trees, originally twelve in number, are essential to maintaining balance in the world, as they filter out negative emotions and combat the corruptive influence of the Ungods.
	The health and color of the Mother Trees serve as a visual indicator of the world's level of corruption. As the trees darken, the spring elves know that it's time to perform rituals using rare herbs and their unique druidic magic. These cleansing ceremonies purify the trees, enabling them to continue their vital work of filtering out corruption.
	Spring elves have round facial features, and their hair is usually brown or dark blond. They are shorter and slimmer but possess more strength than meets the eye.
	Spring elves are led by the Guardians, an elite group of warriors dedicated to defending their home forest. These skilled archers boast exceptional camouflage abilities, blending seamlessly into their surroundings. Some Guardians wield powerful arrows crafted from the branches of the Mother Trees, imbuing their attacks with potent mystical energy. All of their weapons are made from the enchanted wood found only in Sindile.
	In addition to their guardianship duties, spring elves cultivate and nurture the trees that grow in the presence of the Mother Trees. This special care results in the creation of enchanted wood, a resilient and magical material with a wide range of applications. From weapons and shields to ships and buildings, this enchanted wood enables the construction of items far stronger and more durable.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 17 (Indie)

trait.name: Darkvision

trait.name: Trance
trait.text:
Elves don't need to sleep. Instead, they meditate deeply, remaining semiconscious, for 4 hours a day. (The Common word for such meditation is "trance.") While meditating, you can dream after a fashion; such dreams are actually mental exercises that have become reflexive through years of practice. After resting in this way, you gain the same benefit that a human does from 8 hours of sleep.
	If you meditate during a long rest, you finish the rest after only 4 hours. You otherwise obey all the rules for a long rest; only the duration is changed.

trait.name: Ancestral Spring Magic

When you reach 5th level, you learn a 2nd-level druid spell of your choice and can cast it once with this trait. At 7th level, you can cast the speak with plants spell once with this trait. You regain the ability to cast these spells when you finish a long rest. During character creation, you choose whether your spellcasting ability for these spells is Intelligence or Wisdom.

Elven literature is rich and varied, and their songs and poems are famous among other races. Many bards learn their language so they can add Elvish ballads to their repertoires.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
The autumn elves have an innate sense of nobility, exceptional mastery of magic, and a strong sense of duty. Particularly skilled in abjuration, illusion, and wind magic, these elves have honed their abilities to create intricate wards and magically enchanted pylons, setting them apart from other elven subcultures.
	Autumn elves typically possess regal, stern features that convey their sense of nobility and seriousness. With sharp, angular facial structures, they exude an air of authority and wisdom, reflecting their dedication to the magic pursuit and their serious belief in noblesse oblige.
	Their advanced magical prowess has enabled the autumn elves to construct entire flying cities, which showcase their exceptional talent in manipulating reality. By employing arrays of illusions, they can create tangible mirages, that can be touched or used as real objects, that can defy the laws of physics, provide individuals with the power of flight through illusory wings, and even conjure mythical servant creatures that possess combat capabilities.
	To maintain their cities' unique defenses and magical constructs, autumn elves must periodically shift their cities to the Penumbral Plane and harvest mystical energy from penumbral creatures. Elite groups of mystical knights, often supported by mercenaries and adventurers, are tasked with this vital responsibility.
	Aibidh, the Lord of Autumn and King of Wind, bestows the most accomplished mystical knights with stormbirds as their steeds. These elemental creatures of the storm serve as loyal and powerful mounts, further enhancing the noble warriors' combat prowess and ability to navigate the treacherous Penumbral Plane.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 18 (Indie)

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
The winter elves and the kemets, two factions of the same species, share a common origin but differ in their goals and beliefs. Their dark, grayish, or purple skin and contrasting white hair complement their incredible strength, which belies their slender frames. Their proud, cold, and obstinate demeanor reflects their advanced culture, characterized by patience, wisdom, and an acceptance of death.
	The Elf Migrations led these beings to settle in the frigid region of Reginheraht, where they became known as winter elves. They sought power and knowledge to purify their goddess Bás of corruption and restore her benevolent nature. This quest led them to explore various planes, including the Penumbral Plane, where dark entities manipulated them. The winter elves discovered a prophecy foretelling the world's end at the hands of the Ungods, stating that the kemets must conquer the world to prevent this fate. Desperate and recognizing elements of the prophecy in their reality, they changed their name to kemets and resolved to fulfill the prophecy.
	The kemets adopted a militaristic society, subjugating the Kepesh people from the continent of Darkall and seizing their necromantic knowledge. They organized themselves into family clans dwelling in pyramid-shaped structures, symbolizing their mastery over death. The use of undead became commonplace, from menial tasks in their cities to military operations.
	Centuries after conquering Darkall, the kemets invaded Tanares, expecting victory and prophecy fulfillment. However, their invasion failed, and they spiraled into despair, resigned to the world's inevitable end. Bás, the goddess of winter and death, offered them another path. While some kemets deserted, many joined Bás' cult, seeking to create a realm of eternal ice and undeath, impervious to the Ungods' corruption.
	Conversely, those kemets who repented after the war reverted to being called winter elves. Led by Baraelmer, they aim to redeem the kemets and restore Bás' benevolence. They continue to practice necromancy and employ undead, but now honor the dead by only using the bodies of those who permit it after death.
	Baraelmer's winter elves assist the Republic in defending the coasts against the kemet's undead-powered fleet, stationed in the Storm Islands. Their expertise in naval warfare and newly rediscovered water elementalism helps to counter the kemet's advantage at sea.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 19 (Indie)

trait.name: Culture of Necromancy
trait.text:
Only twenty years ago, the winter elves and kemets were a single, united group. However, the failure of the Kemet Invasion caused a schism that split them into distinct factions. Despite this separation, both groups share core cultural traits deeply rooted in necromancy and mastery over death, a knowledge they stole from the Kepesh.
	The living and the undead coexist seamlessly in their cities. Undead horses pull wagons, and mindless undead perform menial tasks like cleaning or guarding locations. This integration into daily life demonstrates how both factions have overcome the fear of death. Moreover, the undead serve a crucial role in their military, forming the backbone of infantry troops. Their emotionless nature and the lack of families and loved ones prevent the Ungods from gaining power when the undeads are destroyed in battle, making them excellent troops to reduce the chances of a Malrokian Curse cataclysm.
	Both winter elves and kemets organize themselves into clan-based societies. Prominent clans reside in massive pyramid-shaped buildings, which serve as both residences and bureaucratic centers. A hierarchy extends from the ancient Patriarchs and Matriarchs at the summit to lower-ranking members at the base, where public offices and accessible areas can be found.
	Though the winter elves and kemets have diverged in beliefs and goals, their necromantic practices remain a key element of their cultures. The winter elves, now allied with the Republic of Freelands, are relearning their ancient water elementalism and using their necromancy and naval knowledge to battle Gullog's forces. They have recently formed a close bond with the Celestianist clerics of Bauron to exchange information on undead control and elimination. Conversely, the kemets embrace the evil tainted ice elementalism, wielding it to empower their undead hordes. Their shared foundation in necromancy continues to shape both factions, even as they carve out unique paths in the aftermath of the Kemet Invasion.

trait.name: Description
trait.text:
Bearers of two souls and two personalities, these angel-like beings organize themselves in knightly orders dedicated to eradication of the Ungods and to accomplish their divine calling.

"We do not hail from the heavens, yet we carry a celestial man date. We have savored the bliss of serenity and divine favor, as well as the harshness of adversity and decay. As each sun rises, we venture into fresh encounters and acquire precious insights that we ought to cherish and impart. Just as a single feather cannot take flight, but a pair can, dual spirits must unite to uncover that which remains hidden from plain sight."
— Zafara, Elder of the Order of Celestial Balance.

In a realm beset by insidious corruption, the cirrus arise as unwavering guardians against the relentless encroachment of malevolence. These celestial-like beings, akin to angels, captivate with their clear blue skin and the majestic wings of their elders. The cirrus embodies the duality of arcane and divine forces, as two souls meld within a single form, intertwining the stark contrast of light and darkness into an unbreakable bond.
	Held together by honor, the cirrus adhere to a stringent code of chivalry and virtues, each exemplified by the unique orders of the Zephyr Knights. These orders represent the cirrus' unfaltering commitment to the essential principles bestowed by the gods, forging a unified front against the otherworldly monstrosities known as the Ungods.
	To the cirrus, the dichotomy of arcane and divine magic transcends mere choice in spellcasting, representing the very essence of their duality. Arcane symbolizes logic, reality, and physicality, while divine signifies wisdom, spirituality, and transcendence. This harmonious equilibrium permeates every facet of their lives, shaping their beliefs and guiding their actions in the ceaseless battle against the forces of insanity emanating from the Penumbral Plane.
	The unity of all Zephyr Knight Orders, distinguished by unique colors and virtues, forges the cirrus into an indomitable force against the Ungods. Through their mastery of arcane and divine energies, they display an unrivaled command of magic, reinforced by their unfaltering dedication to their cause. Amidst adversity, the cirrus stand strong, their unity forming an impervious bulwark against the corrupt ing influence of the Ungods. Though their various knightly orders may harbor diverse opinions and occasionally clash, the Zephyr Knights remain united in their battle against the sinister eldritch beings.
	The celestial nature of the cirrus transcends mere aesthetics; it instills within them an innate sense of purpose, guiding their crusade against the encroaching darkness. As embodiments of balance and harmony, they comprehend the significance of divine order and strive to reestablish equilibrium where corruption seeks to take root. In their youth, each cirrus experiences a divine revelation, imbued with a virtue they must embody and pursue throughout their lives. This revelation directs their path, and the majority join a Zephyr Knight order aligned with their bestowed virtue. Cirrus who abstain from joining an order at adulthood become outcasts, living in exile from their kin and seeking their life's meaning independently. Some reject their calling, while others embrace it further, believing their destiny lies beyond the preconceptions and dogmatism of the orders.
	Their foes, the abhorrent Ungods, represent a desecration of existence, a force the cirrus have vowed to eliminate. These extraplanar deities radiate a corrupting influence, intent on unraveling the fabric of reality and heralding an age of mad ness. Against this unfathomable menace, the cirrus stand resolute, united under the banners of their knight orders and driven by the unwavering conviction of ultimate triumph.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 34 (Indie)

trait.name: Cirrus History
trait.text:
In the dawn of the Godly Age, when angelic hands aid ed sculpting the foundations of creation, the cirrus species emerged—blessed with celestial grace by the angels and entrusted to share the divine word among mortals. However, destiny's path twisted, and they were summoned to war against the looming darkness of the Ungods. As the Ungod Invasion began, the cirrus mustered their unwavering faith and resisted the malevolent tide. Yet, faith alone proved insufficient; they were driven to forge weapons, establish knightly orders, and ultimately, unravel the enigmas of magic and wizardry. Thus, the cirrus unveiled their true potential, merging arcane prowess with divine conviction to confront the Ungods' servants. The Zephyr Knight Orders were born, eternal adversaries of the Ungods.
	The cirrus, as the first denizens of Tanares to wield magic, taught other species the gods' will and the potency of arcane arts after the initial Ungod invasion. Guided by Zafara, a revered elder, the cirrus significantly contributed to the ascension of the Malrokian Kingdom, endorsing its quest for unity and prosperity. Yet the Ungods' insidious corruption infiltrated the kingdom's heart, heedless of the cirrus' dire warnings. The blind nobility instigated a catastrophic war, inflicting untold suffering upon their people, empowering the Ungods, and ultimately unleashing a cataclysm that fractured the continent and nearly eradicated all civilizations. The cirrus were unjustly vilified for the kingdom's demise, their mastery of arcane magic twisted into a malevolent force responsible for the Malrokian Curse. Persecuted and exiled, the cirrus retreated to distant mountains, vowing to avoid further strife.
	As the mournful shroud of the Fallen and Imperial Ages covered the world, the cirrus withdrew into isolation, refining their knowledge and abilities within their hidden sanctuaries. When the Kemet Invasion threatened to unravel the fabric of their world, they emerged from seclusion, wielding their arcane and divine prowess as a bastion against encroaching darkness. The cirrus fought with valor, striving to avert an other Malrokian Curse that could obliterate their world.
	In the present age, the cirrus serve as enigmatic and formidable guardians, their unwavering devotion to their celestial mission shaping their actions. Amidst a world teetering on the brink of ruin, they symbolize virtue and chivalry, resolute protectors against the relentless threat of the Ungods.
	The seven Zephyr Knight Orders epitomize the cirrus species, their distinct virtues and combat techniques bolstering their collective might. Complex webs of loyalty, rivalry, and collaboration interlace a vibrant tapestry of unity among them. Their enduring faith in the gods, coupled with an ancient mastery of both arcane and divine magic, readied the Cirrus to confront the omnipresent darkness. United in their celestial purpose and unyielding in their commitment, they stand vigilant to safeguard the fragile balance of their world. Shaped by divine will and hardened by adversity, the cirrus bear the undeserved stigma of their people, distrusted by many, even as they valiantly defend the mortal realms from the insidious corruption of the Ungods.

trait.name: The First Spellcasters
trait.text:
Throughout the annals of history, the cirrus have distin guished themselves as the first mortals to pray for the gods, and the earliest scholars to unearth the secrets of wizardry. They seamlessly interlaced magic into the essence of their civilization, forging a society where the might of arcane arts and divine power is entwined with their chivalrous way of life.
	Renowned for their mastery of all forms of magic and their unyielding determination to obliterate the Ungods and their nefarious servants, the cirrus strive to pierce the enigmatic Tanarean Magic Field. They believe that this untamed and raw power holds the key to vanquishing the Ungods once and for all. While many other species consider this a great taboo, for the gods themselves established the Tanaren Magic Field, no condemnation has ever deterred the cirrus from pursuing their belief in this divine mandate to find ultimate magic power.
	The chivalric orders of the cirrus exemplify their ingenious and diverse mastery of magic. Each order embodies a unique fusion of virtues and magical expertise, reflecting the rich complexity of cirrus society. Orders bearing black banners excel in arcane spellcasting, while those with white banners champion divine spells. As per time-honored tradition, every cirrus is expected to join one of these orders upon reaching adulthood, undergoing rigorous training as squires before ascending to the esteemed ranks of knights. Though most embrace the path of spellcasting, not all choose this calling; many cirrus adeptly balance their magical prowess with formidable physical combat skills.
	Magic is woven into the very fabric of cirrus culture, molding their society and their relentless battle against the Ungods. Their insatiable thirst for arcane knowledge and divine wisdom has led them to craft potent rituals, capable of decimating their foes and shielding their people. The cirrus' groundbreaking utilization of magic has bestowed upon them a distinct advantage in their ongoing conflict against the Ungods, and their unyielding determination to unravel the enigma of the Tanarean Magic Field bears witness to their unrelenting pursuit of ultimate triumph.
	As a species that has constructed its very existence upon the foundation of magic, the cirrus exemplifies the limitless potential of arcane and divine power.

trait.name: Sharing A Body
trait.text:
The two forms of a cirrus are unique, each considering the other form as another part of their being. For a cirrus, it is so natural to share two forms that they find it strange that individuals of other species are always the same person. 

	• A cirrus always treats their other form as a distinct person, and it is common to hear them say things like "Oh, Torrus did that again?" or "This is something that Arven would love to see."

	• A cirrus is aware of their short time in each form and makes the most of the time before the other form takes over. 

	• Cirrus remember the day lived by the other form as if they had seen the situations in the third person, as mere spectators of the other's life. That's why many of them like to talk to the other form out loud so that the other form can hear them. If they prefer to be discreet, they write a note or something similar. 

	• It is quite common for the two forms to have different functions and responsibilities, understanding that each is, in fact, a different being. Generally, one form of cirrus does not take responsibility for the actions of the other form, as they consider themselves unique beings, and sometimes they disagree with each other's decisions, al though they often agree on some things that require their body to commit daily, such as adventuring in a group or belonging to a team. 

	• The sense of urgency is common among cirrus, as they know that their actions must be limited to a single day. They are generally respectful and have a lot of love for one form to the other, despite the enormous differences, because they understand that they are codependent.

trait.name: Cirrus Names
trait.text:
Simulating the sound of the wind, the vast majority of cirrus names have one (or more) "S" sounds. In addition, they prefer vowels, which "run free" in the air, than hard, truncated, and ephemeral consonants.

Male Names: Assiz, Ossaez, Sans, Sayöes, Saëzz, Zianis, Zarekis, Zenthar, Szarion, Szarys, Zeraxus, Zythas, Zelaris, Sazriel, Zephys, Szalyn, Zorinax.

Female Names: Aziza, Sarah, Sazis, Se-ena, Siff, Zafara, Zoe, Zoza, Sylzara, Zaelis, Sazira, Zarithas, Sylzeth, Zorintha, Sylzana, Szanara, Sylzix.

Clan Names: They carry a title such as Skyborn or Fallenangel. Additionally, if they are a follower of the Windspeakers, they may also indicate which of the Four Winds they belong to.

trait.name: Two In One
Ability Score Increase
trait.text:
In one of your character sheets, increase one ability score by 2 and another ability score by 1. Do the same in the other character sheet, but with different abilities from the two chosen in the first.

	• The two stats you increased on the first sheet cannot be chosen on the other sheet (if you placed 1 on Dexterity on sheet A, you can't place 1 or 2 on Dexterity on sheet B).

trait.text: In their Tamerian form, cirrus tend to be loyal. Already in their Bauronean form, cirrus pull towards chaotic personalities.
